Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS) 2022
checklist, completed for: Cost-Minimization of Endometrial Biopsy
Strategies for Lynch Syndrome Surveillance.

Per the journal's request, the far-right column below does not merely name a
section -- it quotes the actual sentence(s) from the manuscript that satisfy
each item, so a reviewer can verify the claim without searching the text.

| Topic | No. | Item | Reported in section (supporting text) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title | 1 | Identify the study as an economic evaluation and specify the interventions compared. | **Title.** "Cost-Minimization of Endometrial Biopsy Strategies for Lynch Syndrome Surveillance." **Abstract, Objective.** "To estimate and compare the health-system costs of three strategies for endometrial cancer surveillance in women with Lynch syndrome: standalone office endometrial biopsy, operative dilation and curettage (D&C), and endometrial biopsy performed during an already-scheduled surveillance colonoscopy." |
| Abstract | 2 | Provide a structured summary that highlights context, key methods, results, and alternative analyses. | **Abstract, Methods.** "We conducted deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses (1,000 Monte Carlo draws), a threshold analysis, a budget-impact analysis, a geographic sensitivity analysis using real Medicare Geographic Practice Cost Indices and hospital wage indices across four localities, and two supplementary clinical-outcome sensitivity analyses testing the model's assumption of equivalent diagnostic effectiveness across strategies." |
| Background and objectives | 3 | Give the context for the study, the study question, and its practical relevance. | **Introduction, final paragraph.** "We built a decision-analytic, cost-minimization model to estimate and compare the health-system costs of these three strategies, and to test, rather than assume, whether the model's cost conclusion depends on the assumption of equivalent diagnostic effectiveness across strategies, on Medicare-derived parameter uncertainty, or on practice location." |
| Health economic analysis plan | 4 | State whether a health economic analysis plan was developed and where available. | **Methods, opening paragraph.** "No prespecified health economic analysis plan was registered before the analysis began; complete parameter-level sourcing is provided as supplementary material." |
| Study population | 5 | Describe characteristics of the study population and why relevant for decision-making. | **Methods, opening paragraph.** "...adult women with Lynch syndrome who are candidates for gynecologic surveillance and have an already-scheduled surveillance colonoscopy... Age, genotype, menopausal status, and prior biopsy history were not modeled separately; the model represents a single surveillance episode rather than a specific patient subgroup." |
| Setting and location | 6 | Provide relevant contextual information for decision-making. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "Healthcare resources were valued primarily using Medicare allowed amounts (the Physician Fee Schedule and the Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider and Service Public Use Files)..." **Methods, geographic-sensitivity paragraph.** "...we re-priced all three strategies at four localities: the national average, a mid-cost state, a low-cost locality, and a high-cost locality." |
| Comparators | 7 | Describe the interventions being compared and why chosen. | **Methods, opening paragraph.** "...standalone office endometrial biopsy, operative dilation and curettage (D&C), and endometrial biopsy performed during that colonoscopy (combined biopsy). Transvaginal ultrasound was not modeled as a fourth comparator: NCCN's own guideline states that transvaginal ultrasound has not been shown to have sufficient sensitivity or specificity to support a screening recommendation in this population, in contrast to endometrial biopsy." **Introduction.** "...whether this combined approach is also less costly to the health system than the two existing alternatives -- standalone office biopsy or operative dilation and curettage (D&C) -- once the full cost of an escalation to D&C after a failed sampling attempt is accounted for in each strategy." |
| Perspective | 8 | State the perspective(s) adopted and why relevant, and how costs and outcomes assessed were justified. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "The analysis took a U.S. healthcare-sector perspective. Healthcare resources were valued primarily using Medicare allowed amounts... supplemented by published resource-cost estimates for services not separately reimbursed, such as incremental procedure-room and anesthesia time and scheduling-coordination labor. Patient time, transportation, lost productivity, and other nonmedical costs were excluded." |
| Time horizon | 9 | State the time horizon and why appropriate. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "The analytic horizon was a single endometrial-surveillance episode, beginning with the initial sampling strategy and extending through any rescue D&C required after an unsuccessful initial attempt; costs or consequences beyond resolution of that episode were not included." |
| Discount rate | 10 | Report discount rates and why appropriate. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "Because the horizon was less than one year, costs were not discounted." |
| Selection of outcomes | 11 | Describe what outcomes were used and why. | **Methods, third paragraph.** "Total expected cost per patient was the primary outcome, selected because the decision this model addresses... is, in the base case, a cost-minimization question... we selected two secondary outcomes -- D&C-related adverse-event exposure and delayed-neoplasia probability -- specifically to test, rather than merely assume, this equivalence." |
| Measurement of outcomes | 12 | Describe how outcomes were measured. | **Methods, clinical-outcome-sensitivity paragraph.** "...we estimated each strategy's exposure to D&C-related adverse events (a composite of uterine perforation, cervical false passage, and severe hemorrhage, pooled from a cohort of 5,359 nonobstetric D&Cs) as a function of that strategy's probability of ultimately requiring D&C, either as the primary procedure or as a rescue procedure after a failed sampling attempt." **Methods, decision-tree paragraph.** "After a failed office attempt, we modeled two pathways rather than assuming universal escalation to D&C: a repeat office attempt, estimated to occur in 5% of failures... succeeding 75% of the time... or direct escalation to D&C." **Figure 1** shows the structural pathway used to derive these estimates. **Methods, clinical-outcome-sensitivity paragraph (secondary check).** "As a separate, deterministic check on the same equivalent-effectiveness assumption, we also computed each strategy's overall probability of detecting a true cancer or endometrial hyperplasia, combining each arm's sampling-escalation probabilities with published Pipelle and D&C sensitivities from a general (non-Lynch) diagnostic-accuracy meta-analysis. This calculation is a point estimate only, not integrated into the probabilistic sensitivity analysis." |
| Valuation of outcomes | 13 | Describe the population and methods used to value outcomes. | **Methods, third paragraph.** "Both secondary outcomes are reported as event counts per 1,000 patients; neither was converted to a utility, quality-adjusted life-year, or monetary value, so no outcome valuation step was required for them." |
| Measurement and valuation of resources and costs | 14 | Describe how costs were measured and valued. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "Healthcare resources were valued primarily using Medicare allowed amounts... supplemented by published resource-cost estimates for services not separately reimbursed..." **Methods, decision-tree paragraph.** "D&C... cost also includes a partial expected cost for uterine perforation, restricted to the one management pathway (diagnostic laparoscopy) with a cost fully traceable to current Medicare payment data, weighted by that pathway's observed probability in an independent cohort study of postperforation management." **Table 1** lists the source citation and evidence tier used to value every individual cost input. |
| Currency, price date, and conversion | 15 | State the currency, price date, and conversion methods. | **Methods, second paragraph.** "All costs are reported in 2026 U.S. dollars; costs originally reported in an earlier year were inflation-adjusted using the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for Medical Care." |
| Rationale and description of model | 16 | Describe the type of model, why chosen, and provide a diagram if applicable. | **Methods, fourth paragraph.** "Each strategy was modeled as a one-step decision tree: an initial sampling attempt, which either succeeds or fails and escalates to operative D&C... The combined-biopsy arm was modeled under an incremental-cost principle: because the patient is assumed to be undergoing the surveillance colonoscopy regardless of whether biopsy is added, no colonoscopy base cost... was charged to this arm." **Figure 1** is the corresponding decision-tree diagram, built directly from live model output. |
| Analytics and assumptions | 17 | Describe methods to validate/adjust the model and structural assumptions. | **Methods, five-analyses paragraph.** "We conducted five complementary sensitivity analyses. First, deterministic one-way sensitivity analysis... Second, probabilistic sensitivity analysis... Third, threshold analysis... Fourth, scenario analysis... Fifth, budget-impact analysis..." **Methods, validation paragraph.** "We compared the model's cost estimates against three independently published analyses as a validation check..." **Table 1** documents every structural assumption's source and evidence tier. |
| Characterizing heterogeneity | 18 | Describe methods for estimating differential results by subgroups. | **Methods, penultimate paragraph.** "The geographic sensitivity analysis characterizes setting-level heterogeneity (how the base-case conclusion varies by practice location); it does not characterize patient-level heterogeneity, which was not modeled -- the model does not stratify results by age, genotype, menopausal status, or other individual patient characteristics." |
| Characterizing distributional effects | 19 | Describe how impacts were distributed across affected individuals, if analyzed. | **Methods, penultimate paragraph.** "Distributional or equity effects (e.g., differential access or affordability across patient subgroups) were outside this analysis's scope." |
| Characterizing uncertainty | 20 | Describe methods for characterizing parameter and model uncertainty. | **Methods, five-analyses paragraph.** "First, deterministic one-way sensitivity analysis varied each of ten parameters individually across its low/high bound... Second, probabilistic sensitivity analysis drew 1,000 Monte Carlo samples, with each parameter sampled from a distribution matched to its evidence type... Third, threshold analysis solved for the parameter value at which the combined strategy's cost advantage over office biopsy would be lost." |
| Engagement with patients and other affected groups | 21 | Describe steps to engage patients/service recipients/caregivers, and how their perspectives were integrated. | **Methods, penultimate paragraph.** "Structural modeling assumptions describing actual clinical workflow (e.g., whether the combined-biopsy strategy requires a separate preoperative office visit) were informed by clinician-investigator practice experience; no formal patient or public engagement process was undertaken in developing this model." |
| Study parameters | 22 | Report all analytic inputs with ranges/distributions and sources. | **Table 1** caption. "Model parameters: base-case value, low/high bound, distribution, source citation, and evidence tier for every parameter in the model." *Source:* `tables/manuscript_table1_parameters.csv`. |
| Summary of main results | 23 | Report mean values for costs, effects, and their differences, and summarize in a table. | **Results, first paragraph.** "In the base case, combined biopsy cost an estimated $506.11 per patient, compared with $749.18 for standalone office biopsy and $3,839.81 for operative D&C. Combined biopsy was $243.06 (32.4%) less expensive than office biopsy..." **Table 2** summarizes cost and clinical-outcome means by strategy. |
| Effect of uncertainty | 24 | Describe how uncertainty in study inputs affected findings. | **Results.** "Across 1,000 probabilistic-sensitivity draws, combined biopsy had a mean cost of $539.93 (SD $116.01) and office biopsy a mean cost of $755.70 (SD $119.99). Combined biopsy was the least expensive strategy in 91.4% of draws; D&C was never the least expensive strategy in any draw." **Results, geographic paragraph.** "Combined biopsy remained the least expensive strategy in all four localities tested." |
| Effect of engagement with patients and others | 25 | Report the results of engagement, if any. | **Methods, penultimate paragraph.** Same sentence as item 21, naming the specific structural assumption -- whether the combined arm requires a separate preoperative office visit -- that clinician-investigator input affected, since no formal patient/public engagement was undertaken. |
| Study findings, limitations, generalizability, and current knowledge | 26 | Report key findings, limitations, generalizability, and how the study fits with current knowledge. | **Discussion, second paragraph.** "This model's principal limitation is that its cost-minimization design formally assumes equivalent diagnostic effectiveness across strategies. We tested that assumption two ways, with different results. First, whether a failed sample goes entirely undiagnosed... This is a genuine absence of evidence for a differential risk, not evidence the risks are equal... Second, each strategy's overall detection probability for a true cancer or precancer, combining escalation probabilities with published (non-Lynch) Pipelle and D&C sensitivities, suggested D&C's point estimate exceeds office and combined biopsy's (see Results) -- but D&C's own sensitivity carries a 95% confidence interval spanning 28.1%-99.3%, so this difference is far from established." **Discussion, closing paragraph.** "Endometrial biopsy performed during an already-scheduled surveillance colonoscopy costs less, and exposes patients to less D&C-related procedural risk, than either standalone office biopsy or operative D&C for Lynch syndrome surveillance. This conclusion was robust to parameter uncertainty and practice location in every sensitivity analysis performed." |
| Source of funding | 27 | Describe funding source(s), role of funder, and how it influenced the study. | **Title Page.** "Disclosure of funding received for this work: [State any funding from organizations such as NIH, or state 'No funding was received for this work.']" The reporting field exists; the author has not yet supplied the actual funding statement, so no sentence can be quoted as satisfied yet. |
| Conflicts of interest | 28 | Report authors' conflicts of interest per journal policy. | **Title Page.** "Disclosure of financial support: [State any source of financial support for the study, including supplies or services from a commercial organization, or state 'The authors did not report any potential conflicts of interest.']" The reporting field exists; the author has not yet supplied the actual disclosure, so no sentence can be quoted as satisfied yet. |
